get.description:
Bulk odds for a sport. Filter by market keys (comma-separated).

Served through a short-TTL single-flight cache — this is the single
highest-volume read path (48% of peak-hour traffic on the 2026-08-08 record
day) and the response is tier-independent. See api/odds_cache.py for the
TTL rationale. No `session` dependency: the loader opens its own read
session so a cancelled leader request can't poison coalesced callers.

Returns a pre-rendered `Response`, so FastAPI skips `response_model`
validation and re-serialization on the hot path — that step measured
0.22-0.48s of BLOCKING event-loop time per ~2 MB response and was being paid
on cache HITS too. `response_model` is kept for the OpenAPI schema only;
`odds_cache.render_odds_json` reproduces its output byte for byte (see that
function before changing any model in this response tree).

parameters.name: includeBookIds

schema.description: When true, each bookmaker block carries `book_event_id` (that book's own event identifier) and every outcome carries `book_outcome_id` (that book's own selection/contract id) plus `outcome_id` (PropLine's own canonical outcome id — the same value `line_movement` / `resolution` webhooks carry, so a push delivery joins onto exactly one REST row). Use these to join PropLine rows onto a book's native feed without matching on team names, players and lines. Kalshi ships both — the event ticker and the per-contract market ticker (e.g. KXMLBGAME-26AUG08NYYBOS-NYY). Books that don't publish a stable id return null. PropLine-specific; both fields are always present in the response shape and are null unless this param is set (same convention as `link`/`includeLinks`), so no existing consumer's parsing changes.

parameters.name: includePregameOnly

parameters.name: includeRestricted

schema.description: PrizePicks marks some projections over-only (its own `allowed_wager_types`), and in some states the Under is still available. get.description:
Get odds for a single event — supports player prop markets.
This is where the real value is.

Default `markets` is `h2h,spreads,totals` — the three game-line
markets every book carries across every sport. Pass an explicit
`markets=` to fetch player props (sport-specific keys like
pitcher_strikeouts / player_points / player_goals).
Previous default was MLB-only and silently returned 0 bookmakers
on every other sport when the caller (or SDK) omitted the param.

get.description:
List available market types for a specific event.
Useful for discovering what props are available before requesting odds.

Counts STORED offerings: full-game markets only, and a retired book's
rows only on a completed event (the same two cuts /odds makes that SQL
can express). /odds additionally withholds prices a book has withdrawn
or stopped delivering (outcome_unseen, market_dark, stale siblings,
impossible rungs, superseded period twins), so these counts can be
higher than what /odds serves — use /odds for what is live. Measured
2026-09-25: MLB 228432 10,962 stored vs 6,537 served. Deliberately NOT
computed through the /odds formatter: that measured ~2s per cache miss
on a heavy event against ~40ms for this query, on an endpoint polled
~100x/min.

Historical odds movement for a single event.
Paid tiers (Hobby / Pro / Streaming Lite / Streaming / Enterprise):
full snapshot history. Free tier: redacted (shows structure and count).

get.description:
Line movement + steam detection, derived from our snapshot tick history.

For each (book, market, outcome) returns the opening line, the latest
line, and the implied-probability / point shift between them. The
top-level ``steam`` array flags outcomes that multiple books moved in
the same direction — the classic sharp-money signal, computed across
all 16 books we poll. No competitor offers this (they're pull-only).

Paid tiers (Hobby+): full data. Free tier: redacted (structure only).

get.description:
List futures markets for a sport — championship winner, MVP,
division winner, etc. One row per (futures event, book, market) with
every team or player priced. Free tier; pulled from each book's
futures feed (Bovada today). Order is by event commence_time
(typically season-end) ascending.

Optional `?bookmakers=` (comma-separated book keys) narrows the
per-book market rows to those books — same the-odds-api-compatible
contract as every /odds endpoint: omitted = all books, unknown keys
match nothing. A futures event with no market left after filtering is
dropped so consumers never get an empty `markets: []` row.

get.description:
Game conditions: probable pitchers, confirmed-lineup flag, the
home-plate umpire, and first-pitch weather (outdoor / open-roof venues).

The context a prop settles under — joined into /results so every graded
outcome carries its conditions. Free tier. MLB today; weather extends
to other outdoor sports next. Returns 404 if no context is on file yet
(e.g. before the context loop has reached the event, or for sports
without a context source).

Compute cross-book +EV for a single event.

`markets` is an optional comma-separated filter. If omitted, every
market on the event is evaluated. Each market line that has Pinnacle
(preferred) or Bovada (fallback) coverage gets a no-vig fair price
and an EV% per book.

`bookmakers` is an optional comma-separated book-key filter
(the-odds-api-compatible, same as on the odds endpoints) — shop only
the books you hold accounts at.

IMPORTANT: the filter narrows the PRICES you get back. It never
narrows the fair-line anchor. The no-vig fair price still comes from
the sharp book (Pinnacle → Polymarket → Kalshi → Bovada), so
`bookmakers=draftkings` still returns DraftKings EV% measured against
Pinnacle — the whole point of the endpoint. Filtering the anchor away
instead would leave every line unpriceable and return nothing.
`fair_source` on each line always names the anchor actually used,
filtered or not. Lines where none of your books quote a price are
omitted.

parameters.name: devig

schema.description: How the anchor's vig is removed before the fair line is derived. 'multiplicative' (default) divides each implied probability by the booksum, spreading the overround evenly. 'shin' solves Shin's insider-trading model, which loads the overround onto the longshot side and so corrects the favourite-longshot bias — the difference is negligible on a -110/-110 total and material on a +600 anytime scorer. The default is the only method the +EV backtest is measured on.

parameters.name: fair_source

schema.description: Choose the fair-line anchor: one or more of pinnacle, polymarket, kalshi, bovada, smarkets, comma-separated, tried in that order. Default pinnacle → polymarket → kalshi → bovada → smarkets. Lines none of the chosen anchors price are omitted. Or 'consensus': the median no-vig probability across every book quoting a clean, fresh two-sided market (3+ books; same-feed siblings count once). Each line then lists the books used in `fair_books`.

get.description:
Calculate EV% for a user-supplied price against the event's no-vig
fair anchor.

Useful when you bet at a book PropLine doesn't carry directly
(Caesars, BetMGM, Fanatics, BetUS, Hard Rock, etc.). The fair line
is derived from the same Pinnacle-preferred anchor as the bulk
`/ev` endpoint, so the math is identical — you're just plugging in

get.description:
Per-bookmaker freshness — `last_update` summary across all markets.

Returns:
    bookmakers: [
      { key, market_count, latest_update, staleness_seconds, is_stale,
        worst_staleness_seconds, suspended_market_count,
        market_classes: {
          game_lines: { market_count, latest_update, staleness_seconds,
                        active_market_count, oldest_market_update,
                        worst_staleness_seconds, suspended_market_count },
          props:      { ...same shape },
        } }
    ]
    stale_threshold_seconds
    as_of (server time the rows were sampled)

`staleness_seconds` is the time since the most recent successful
market write for the book — a rough proxy for "how fresh is the
freshest line on this book." It overstates per-event freshness
because any single market touch resets it; for the marketing page
that's fine since the public claim we're backing is "we ingest
book data continuously and recently."

`market_classes` splits that per class (game lines vs props) so a class
going dark behind fresh game lines — the Pinnacle 2026-08-02 prop
incident — is visible here too. Single grouped query, no Event join, so
unlike the monitor's query this split does NOT exclude futures markets
(they land under `props` and can keep it looking fresher than the
per-game prop board really is) — acceptable for a trust surface.

A third `futures` class was considered (sportsapis.dev review follow-up,
2026-08-27) and deliberately NOT added, for two reasons that compound:
(1) `futures` is an `Event.is_future` property, not a `Market.key`
property, so `market_class_case()` — which buckets on `Market.key` alone
and is SHARED with the monitor — cannot emit it without an Event join in
every caller. And the monitor (`sport_book_class_freshness_rows`)
deliberately EXCLUDES futures so a year-round-fresh outright can't mask a
dark prop parse, so it can never carry a futures class: "keep the
vocabulary shared with the monitor" and "add a futures class" are
mutually exclusive on the same shared expression. (2) Splitting futures
out of props *correctly* (props excluding futures) forces an Event join
into THIS first query, which is deliberately join-free and spans every
market in the DB — not the bounded active-board window the ~167ms cost
was measured on. The worst-case fields (`worst_staleness_seconds` et al.)
ALREADY exclude futures via the active-board Event join, so the only
residual is a mildly inflated headline `props` count/latest on a trust
page — already noted as acceptable above. Net: high coupling + unbounded
cost to fix a cosmetic inflation. Skipped on purpose.

Each class (and the book) also carries the WORST case:
`worst_staleness_seconds` / `oldest_market_update` — the age of the
oldest NON-SUSPENDED market on the active board (events from -6h to
+48h) — plus `active_market_count` and `suspended_market_count`.
Headline staleness answers "is the book being ingested"; worst-case
answers "is any individual market being silently missed". A market
with `suspended_at` set is excluded from the worst-case number because
a flagged withdrawal is not a capture hole (the book pulled it; we
keep its last price and say so on /odds). Second grouped query with an
Event join, bounded by the active-board window.

authenticated request 500'd — and the public status page, which watches
`/health`, said Operational. This is the endpoint that page should watch.
Accepts HEAD because UptimeRobot's free tier can only send HEAD (a paid
plan is needed to choose GET), and every `/v1` route 405s on HEAD.

It reads two settings and writes nothing (no usage_logs row, no auth), so
it is safe to poll and cannot itself fail on a read-only primary. A
connection failure is also 503: the write address is not serving.

BestLineOut.title: BestLineOut
BestLineOut.description: One (market_key, player, point) tuple with the best price per side.

BestLineSideOut.title: BestLineSideOut
BestLineSideOut.description:
Best price + every alternative for one side of a market line.

`best` is the highest American price across the books returning a
valid quote for this side. `all_prices` is the same set sorted
best-first (one row per book), so consumers can show runner-ups
without a second request. DFS pick'em books (PrizePicks, Sleeper,
Dabble) are excluded — their quotes aren't independently bettable
payouts; Underdog is included only at its clean two-way lines
(payout_multiplier == 1.0), same rule as /ev.

BestPriceOut.title: BestPriceOut
BestPriceOut.description: A single book's price at a given line. Used in best-line responses.

ClvBetIn.title: ClvBetIn
ClvBetIn.description: One placed bet to be graded against its closing line.

DepthLevelOut.title: DepthLevelOut
DepthLevelOut.description:
One order-book level BEYOND an outcome's served price (see
OutcomeOut.depth).

EvCalcOut.title: EvCalcOut
EvCalcOut.description: User-supplied price evaluated against the event's no-vig fair anchor.

EventBestLineOut.title: EventBestLineOut
EventBestLineOut.description: Cross-book best-line response for one event.

GameContextOut.title: GameContextOut
GameContextOut.description:
Conditions a game is played under — the context every prop settles
against. Free tier. MLB today; weather extends to other outdoor
sports next.

HitRateSplitOut.title: HitRateSplitOut
HitRateSplitOut.description:
Over/under split across a fixed look-back window of graded games.

`over_pct` is over / (over + under) — pushes are excluded from the
denominator (standard hit-rate convention). None when the window has
no decisive (non-push) games.

PlayerGameOut.title: PlayerGameOut
PlayerGameOut.description:
One completed game in a player's game log.

`stats` is a flat map of every stat_type recorded for this player in this
game, so a caller gets the whole box-score line in one row rather than one
request per stat. The vocabulary is per-sport — see /docs#stats.

PlayerMarketTrendOut.title: PlayerMarketTrendOut
PlayerMarketTrendOut.description:
Aggregated hit-rate trends for one player in one market — the
"X went over in 7 of his last 10" surface. Derived purely from
PropLine's prop resolution (the-odds-api has no equivalent).

SgpBookErrorOut.title: SgpBookErrorOut
SgpBookErrorOut.description:
One book that could not quote the slip, with the same `detail` the
single-book call would have returned as its error body.

SgpComplementOut.title: SgpComplementOut
SgpComplementOut.description:
`include_hold=true`: the same slip with one leg flipped, priced at
the same book. P(slip) + P(complement) = P(rest of the legs), so their
implied probabilities over the rest's implied probability, minus one,
is the book's hold on this combination (`hold`).

market.title: Market
market.description: Market key as served by /odds, e.g. h2h, totals, batter_1plus_hits.

name.title: Name
name.description: Outcome name as served by /odds: team name, Over/Under, the player for YES-only props, or an 'N+' rung with the player in description. The portable prop form is the primary key + 'N+' + player in description (batter_hits / '2+' / 'Ben Malgeri'): it pins at every book, whichever of the three stored forms that book carries (Over N-0.5, an 'N+' rung, or a per-threshold YES key such as batter_2plus_hits). Only the leading N+ is read; 'Under'/'No' never bridges.

description.title: Description
description.description: Outcome description as served by /odds (the player on a two-way prop); empty for game lines.

point.title: Point
point.description: Line, exactly as served by /odds. Omit for h2h and YES-only props.

period.title: Period
period.description: Canonical period code (q1, h1, f5). Omit for full game.

team.title: Team
team.description: For a TEAM total: the team, as /odds serves it in the market's `team` field. Omit for the game total — a totals leg with no team matches only the team-less market, so the two never collide.

book_outcome_id.title: Book Outcome Id
book_outcome_id.description: The book's own id from ?includeBookIds=true. When given, the other fields are ignored. On betonlineag / lowvig this is Sportcast's settlement id (e.g. MatchWinner_Home).

SgpLegIn.title: SgpLegIn
SgpLegIn.description: One leg, named as `/odds` names it, or by the book's own id.

SgpMultiQuoteOut.title: SgpMultiQuoteOut
SgpMultiQuoteOut.description:
`bookmaker=all`: every supported book quoted on the same legs.

`quotes` holds one full single-book response per book that answered
(in SUPPORTED_BOOKS order); `errors` names each book that did not, with
the status + detail its own call would have raised. `best_bookmaker`
is the quoted book paying the most — the shopping answer, since the
same legs at a smaller correlation reduction are the same bet at a
better price.

bookmaker.title: Bookmaker
bookmaker.description: Book to price at: fanduel, draftkings, betonlineag, lowvig, betrivers, betmgm or unibet — or `all` to quote every supported book side by side.

legs.title: Legs
legs.description: The slip. Send `legs` OR `slips`, not both.

slips.title: Slips
slips.description: Batch: up to 25 slips on this event, priced in one call. Each result carries its own status; one slip failing never fails the request.

include_hold.title: Include Hold
include_hold.description: Also price the complement slip (the last leg that has an opposite side flipped: Over<->Under, Yes<->No, the other team) and report `hold`. Costs one more book call per quote (two when the rest of the slip is itself a parlay); off by default.

bookmaker.title: Bookmaker
bookmaker.description: Book for this slip; defaults to the request's `bookmaker`.

SgpSlipIn.title: SgpSlipIn
SgpSlipIn.description: One slip of a batch: its own legs, and optionally its own book.

SgpSlipResultOut.title: SgpSlipResultOut
SgpSlipResultOut.description:
One slip of a batch. `status` is the HTTP status the single-slip
call would have answered; `quote` is set on 200, `error`/`detail` on
anything else.
